bull.b: Rapid growth in prescriptions, prescribers and treated patients indicates genuine early adoption of CARDAMYST. Emerging repeat use could support a durable commercial base as physician familiarity expands and the product becomes integrated into PSVT treatment.

Broader payer access should reduce prescription denials, co-pay support and gross-to-net pressure. Higher coverage can improve treatment availability and average selling prices, creating a structural foundation for stronger revenue conversion.

Initiating a pivotal trial extends etripamil beyond PSVT into a larger adjacent cardiovascular indication. If successful, this could diversify future revenue and improve the product's commercial leverage, although approval and trial execution remain necessary.

bear.t: Large losses remain far ahead of revenue
bear.b: The company remains deeply unprofitable while revenue is still at an early-launch scale. Sustained operating losses indicate that commercial growth must expand substantially before the business can support its cost base and reduce dependence on external capital.

bear.t: High cash burn and leverage constrain flexibility
bear.b: Heavy cash consumption and elevated debt relative to equity reduce financial flexibility during commercialization. Continued funding needs may require additional borrowing or equity issuance, increasing dilution and execution risk if product uptake develops slowly.

bear.t: Reimbursement and clinical execution remain key dependencies
bear.b: Future growth is not determined solely by prescription demand: payer timing, Medicare access and ASP normalization remain uncertain. In parallel, endpoint and event-classification challenges could delay or weaken AFib-RVR results and limit pipeline expansion.
